questions.text: What is the register map of the test shell (offset, width, reset value and access of every register)?
questions.default: 0x00 ID, 0x04 RX_BYTE, 0x08 TICK, 0x0C TAKE, 0x10 STATUS, 0x14 REPLY_LEN, 0x18 REPLY_IDX, 0x1C REPLY_WORD, 0x20 TELE_LEN, 0x24 TELE_IDX, 0x28 TELE_WORD, all 32-bit, as in registers.map.
questions.reason: The request names registers but gives no offsets.
questions.answer:
IN: offset 0x00, WO, reset 0: [7:0] packet byte, [8] end flag
STAT: offset 0x09, RO, reset 0: [0] telemetry on, [1] busy
RIDX: offset 0x03, RW, reset 0: [6:0] word number
RWORD: offset 0x04, RO, reset 0: bytes 4i..4i+3 of the reply, first byte on top, zero past the end
RLEN: offset 0x02, RO, reset 0: length in bytes of the latest reply, 0 if none
TICK: offset 0x01, WO, reset 0: [7:0] n ticks
TIDX: offset 0x06, RW, reset 0: [6:0] word number
TWORD: offset 0x07, RO, reset 0: same for the telemetry frame
TAKE: offset 0x08, WO, reset 0: any write takes the held telemetry frame
TLEN: offset 0x05, RO, reset 0: length of the held telemetry frame, 0 if none
shell: test shell, PROTOCOL.md 1.1
unmapped: no register at an offset: reads 0, writes ignored (read-only registers behave the same on write)

questions.text: Is the status reply payload length byte 17?
questions.reason: 7 counters of 2 bytes, 2 bytes of frame count and 1 byte flag make 17.
questions.answer: Yes. The STATUS payload is seven 16-bit counters (14 bytes), a 16-bit telemetry frame count (2 bytes), and a TLM_ON byte (1 byte), which totals 17 bytes.
questions.evidence: STATUS: seven 16-bit counters, telemetry frame count (16 bit), TLM_ON byte, all before this command is counted.

questions.text: Is a refused packet's counter for refused-packets register also incremented for silent drops?
questions.default: Yes, every refusal including silent drops counts.
questions.reason: The request says each refused packet counts in the refused-packets register.
questions.answer: Yes. The spec says the first three screening failures (too long, too short, bad check) are silent drops, and that each refusal is counted in one counter and in the refused-packets register.
questions.evidence: the first three are dropped without a reply; each refusal is counted in one counter and in the refused-packets register
